gap: No result ChatGPT got states chamber-heater watts per litre of cabinet. On that measure the QIDI Plus5 is highest (550 W ÷ 136.2 L = 4.04 W/L), well ahead of ChatGPT's pick, the Plus4 (400 W ÷ 135.3 L = 2.96 W/L), and ahead of the Q2 (3.22 W/L) and Max4 (2.53 W/L).
standout_why: I compared against four pages. The cited QIDI Plus4 tech-specs page lists the 400 W chamber line but no other model. desktop3dprinters.us/lists/chamber-temperature-specs (cited) gives only maximum chamber temperatures (65 °C for nearly every model) and has no heater watts, heat-up times or per-volume figures. 3dcalculators.com/blog/heat-3d-printer-enclosure (cited) gives Q2 280 W and Plus4 400 W plus reported Plus4 warm-up times, but has no Plus5 or Max4 wattage and no normalisation by volume. The cited Yakja page would not load (certificate error). None of them divides heater power by chamber size, and none mentions the Plus5's 550 W heater or its 500 W bed.
decides: This changes the pick ChatGPT gave. It named the Plus4 for fastest chamber heat-up, but by the maker's own figures the Plus5 puts 1.37× as much chamber-heater power into almost the same size cabinet (4.04 / 2.96 = 1.37). The Plus5 should therefore warm its chamber fastest of the QIDI line, and Dealectric lists it. This is a power-density proxy, not a measured time. Bambu (H2S, X2D, H2D) and Creality (K2 Plus) don't publish chamber-heater wattage, so the ratio can't rank them; the page should say so rather than guess.

findings.label: Chamber heater watts per litre of cabinet
findings.source_title: QIDI Plus5 TechSpecs – QIDI US Store
findings.note: Rated power '150W+550W(Chamber Heating)+500W(Heatbed)'; printer dimensions 500×488×558 mm. 50.0×48.8×55.8 cm = 136.2 L; 550 W ÷ 136.2 L = 4.04 W/L. External box volume is used as a consistent stand-in for chamber air volume.

findings.label: Bed heater watts per cm² of print area
findings.source_title: QIDI Plus5 TechSpecs – QIDI US Store
findings.note: 500 W heatbed ÷ (32 × 32 cm print area = 1,024 cm²) = 0.49 W/cm². The page also says the bed holds maximum power for about 3–5 minutes so it reaches temperature quickly.

findings.label: Plus5 vs Plus4 chamber power density
findings.source_title: QIDI Plus5 TechSpecs – QIDI US Store
findings.note: 4.04 W/L (Plus5) ÷ 2.96 W/L (Plus4, from https://us.qidi3d.com/pages/qidi-plus-4-techspecs) = 1.37. The two cabinets are nearly the same size (136.2 L vs 135.3 L), so the difference comes from the heater (550 W vs 400 W).
